newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine cen bank withdraws order on Russian bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine cen bank withdraws order on Russian bank.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank temporarily advised Ukrainian banks to close accounts at one of Russia's biggest banks -- but then abruptly withdrew the order.

The original order, issued on Wednesday and confirmed by the central bank's Surveillance Department, said Inkombank -- Russia's third biggest bank by assets -- could experience "further financial difficulties".
It said: "We believe it is vital to propose to commercial banks which have opened accounts at Inkombank to take urgent measures to transfer their funds to other more stable banks."
But a second document issued on Friday withdrew the order "pending a thorough review of previous information by the Russian central bank."
There was no further explanation and Ukrainian central bank officials were unavailable for comment.

In Moscow, Inkombank spokesman Alexander Subbotin said the order amounted to an attempt to discredit the bank "linked to the fact that Inkombank is heavily involved in the Ukrainian market and has established a firm position there".

In its initial order, the Ukrainian central bank said it was issuing the advice on the strength of information provided by Ukraine's Moscow embassy outlining which banks it believed "gave rise to concern and uncertainty".
But an embassy spokesman in Moscow expressed surprise that such an order could be issued on the basis of what was no more than a press review.

Ukrainian banks said they saw no basis for the central bank order. A senior foreign currency official at Privatbank, one of Ukraine's biggest banks, and heavily involved in dealings with Russian banks, said it had met no difficulties with Inkombank.
No one was available to comment on the issue at the Russian central bank.

In July, the Russian central bank issued a statement saying an investigation it had carried out into Inkombank showed that the bank had adequate profitabiliy, creditworthiness and stability, and was able to to meet in full its liabilities to depositors and creditors.
The central bank said Inkombank had been told to correct some violations it had committed in forming its reserve funds, carrying out some operations and in some accounting actions.
